items.e: AND…JUDGE THEM. U-shefatum is to be rendered, and the judges judge them. Our verse is similar to No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge (Deut. 24:6).

DESERVE TO BE BEATEN. The word bin (deserve) is vocalized with a chirik . Compare, bin nun (son of Nun) (Josh. 1:1) and bin yakeh (son of Jakeh) (Prov. 30:1). Bin hakkot (deserve to be beaten) is similar to ben bliyya’al (a base fellow) (I Sam. 25:17). Bin laylah (in a night) in which came up in a night (Jonah 4:10) is similar. The judge is obligated to beat him. I believe that Scripture calls the culprit wicked because he struck his neighbor.
THAT THE JUDGE SHALL CAUSE HIM TO LIE DOWN. By command. The same applies to and to be beaten , as before his face proves.

ACCORDING TO THE MEASURE OF HIS WICKEDNESS, BY NUMBER. Of blows. It would have appeared to us, were it not for the words of tradition, that there are some sins that a person is punished for with ten blows. Others are punished with twenty blows. Other sins are punished with a lesser or greater number. The clause according to the measure of his wickedness is proof of this. In any case, the blows shall not exceed forty. However, the words of tradition alone are true. Others say that his wickedness refers to greater or lesser blows, all of which number forty.

THEN THY BROTHER SHOULD BE DISHONORED. For the thing is well known. It is a decree from the Almighty that the sufferer suffer forty blows. This is a decree from heaven so that the number of blows not depend on the will of the judge.
[WHEN HE TREADETH.] The deniers say that the bet in be-disho (when he treadeth down) indicates prior to treading. However, this is unnecessary.

IF BRETHREN DWELL TOGETHER. The deniers also say that these brethren are not actual brothers, but are relatives. They brought proof from Boaz. However, they contribute nothing, for there is no mention of levirate marriage, only of redemption. Why mention the word together ? Does it matter if they were in one state or in one courtyard, or if they loved each other? They say, look, the verse says ve-yibbemah (and shall perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her). This shows that he is her brother-in-law in name only. It is like thy sister-in-law (yevimtekh) is gone back (Ruth 1:15). Now observe that they have become foolish and stupid, for Scripture states, with regard to the sons of Judah, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother (ve-yabbem) unto her (Gen. 38:8). Now he was her brother-in-law. Also, the term yevimtekh (thy sister-in-law) (Ruth 1:15) was used because they were married to two brothers. All intelligent people know that the negative commandments given to Moses were not previously prohibited. However, it would not have been evil in the eyes of God if someone abstained from them before the law was given to Moses. The fact that Scripture states, for all these abominations have the men of the land done, that were before you (Lev. 18:27), shows that this is certainly the case. We do not find a prophet who warned them. Look, Scripture says of Onan, who did not give seed to his brother, the thing which he did was evil in the sight of God (Gen. 38:10). We will therefore rely on the tradition that they are actual brothers.
AND HAVE NO CHILD. For if the deceased has a son, there is no need for him to take his brother’s wife, for she is forbidden to him.
The word yachdav (together) is to be understood in accordance with the explanation of the transmitters of tradition.
ONE NOT OF HIS KIN. This explains the term ha-chutzah (abroad). This law applies only if the brother-in-law intends to marry her.
THE FIRST-BORN THAT SHE BEARETH. Will be called by the name of his brother.
THAT HIS NAME BE NOT BLOTTED OUT. Scripture speaks of his inheritance. I have previously explained the meaning of that she beareth in my comments on unto a foreign people (Ex. 21:8).
MY HUSBAND’S BROTHER. The yod of yevami (my husband’s brother) is in fact the sign of the object.
AND IF HE STAND, AND SAY. Until the elders hear.
AND LOOSE. Ve-chaletzah (and loose) is similar to chaletzu (draw out) in draw out the breast (Lam. 3:4). Its meaning is to remove.

IN HIS FACE. The transmitters of tradition explain that the word be-fanav (in his face) has the meaning of before his face. According to its plain meaning, be-fanav means before the shoe, for panav here is similar to panim (in front) in front and on the back (Ezek. 2:9).
WHEN MEN STRIVE. The reverse of If brethren dwell together (v. 5). The men spoken of are strangers or brothers.

BY THE SECRETS. Mevushav (the secrets) means his testicles. It is related to the word bushah (shame). It is an act of audacity to uncover that which is hidden, namely, a person’s nakedness. It is also a vital organ.
THEN THOU SHALT CUT OFF HER HAND. If she does not pay ransom money. Its meaning is similar to eye for eye (Ex. 21:24).
THINE EYE SHALL HAVE NO PITY. If she be poor.

IN THY BAG. Where you place the scales. Or, do not deceitfully take the weights from the bag. The first interpretation is correct. The proof text is, Let us all have one hag (kis) (Prov. 1:14), the meaning of which is, one scale. The word kis (bag) is related to the word tachossu (ye shall make your count) in ye shall make your count for the lamb (Ex. 12:4) even though tachossu comes from a different root. Many explained the word kis to mean a pouch. There is no need for this interpretation.
PERFECT. No part shall be missing.
[JUST MEASURE.] A just measure means a measure which conforms to the market measure.
THAT THY DAYS MAY BE LONG. For it is well known that all righteous kingdoms will endure, for righteousness is like a building. However, unrighteousness is like a ruin. Its wall collapses in a moment

FOR ALL THAT DO SUCH THINGS. Those who possess diverse measures and diverse weights. This is followed by a general rule, namely, even all that do unrighteously verbally and by deed, secretly or publicly.
HOW HE MET THEE. Karekha (met thee) is related to the word korot (befallen) in all that had befallen them (Gen. 42:29).

AND SMOTE THE HINDMOST OF THEE. Va-yezanev bekhah (and smote the hindmost of thee) means, and cut off your tail ( zanav ), namely, all that were enfeebled in thy rear , that is, those who did not have the strength to walk. It is possible that the word necheshalim (enfeebled) is similar to nechelashim (enfeebled). Similarly keves (lamb) and kesev (lamb).
WHEN THOU WAS FAINT. For Amalek came to Rephidim where the people thirsted for water. The latter is clearly stated.
AND WEARY. From the way.

AND HE FEARED NOT. This refers to Amalek. Yare (feared) is a verb in the perfect. It is like the word kaved (heavy) in for the thing is too heavy for thee (Ex. 18:8); zaken (old) in that when Isaac was old (Gen. 27:1), and ahev (loveth) in such as he loveth ( Ibid. , 8).

WHEN THE LORD THY GOD HATH GIVEN THEE REST. It means that this commandment takes effect after Israel inherits the land and the land is quiet from all the wars with the surrounding nations, for as long as they are involved in waging war with the nations close to them they are not obligated to fight Amalek.

THAT THOU SHALT BLOT OUT THE REMEMBRANCE. Namely, slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass (I Sam 15:3), so that no one says this ox is from the spoil taken from Amalek. The words of the Torah are a general statement. The words of the prophet Samuel go into detail.
THOU SHALT NOT FORGET. Scripture says this after having already stated Remember… (v. 17) for emphasis. The same is true with many other commandments in the Torah.

AND IT SHALL BE, WHEN THOU ART COME. Since Scripture wrote, Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest (Deut. 25:19), God now says that there are commandments that must be observed before He gives you rest. In fact, these commandments take effect as soon as you enter the land. They are: the first fruits, the tithes, writing the Torah on the stones, building the altar, and the blessing and the curse on the two mountains.

IN A BASKET. Tene (basket) is a basket-like receptacle. The word tanakha (thy basket) (Deut 28:5) is its companion. This commandment is incumbent upon those who are close to the place of the sanctuary.
[THAT SHALL BE IN THOSE DAYS.] In those days means that this law is in force as long as there is a kohen gadol there.
I PROFESS. The reason for this utterance is so that the children will hear. Or it is, like a statement of thanks to God, for He has fulfilled his oath. The fruit is proof of this.

AND THOU SHALT SPEAK. It is possible that the kohanim will ask, “What is this that you brought?” Hence Scripture reads ve-anita (and thou shalt speak). On the other hand, ve-anita may mean, and you shall begin speaking. Compare, And Job spoke (va-ya’an) and said (Job 3:2).

A WANDERING ARAMEAN. The word oved (wandering) is an intransitive verb. If Aramean referred to Laban then Scripture should have read mavid or me’abbed . Furthermore, what reason would Scripture have had for stating, Laban sought to destroy my father and he went down to Egypt ? Laban did not cause Jacob to descend to Egypt. It thus appears to me that the term Aramean refers to Jacob. Scripture, as it were, reads, when my father was in Aram he was “perishing.” That is, he was poor, he had no money. Similarly oved (perish) in Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish (Prov. 31:6). Let him drink, and forget his poverty (Prov. 31:7) is proof. The meaning of our phrase thus is, a perishing Aramean was my father. Its import is, I did not inherit the land from my father, for my father was poor when he came to Aram. He was also a stranger in Egypt. He was few in number. He then became a large nation. You O Lord took us out of slavery and gave us a good land. Let the one who disputes not argue, “How could Jacob be called an Aramean?” Look, we find the same with Ithra the Ishmaelite who, as Scripture clearly states, was an Israelite.

FEW IN NUMBER. The word mete (men of) is in the construct, for it is not found in the singular. The word metim is a plural. Rabbi Jonah the grammarian explained it very well under the entry mem, tav, heh .
OUR AFFLICTION. In lacking wealth.
OUR TOIL. In building.
OUR OPPRESSION. As in [ And the taskmasters] were urgent, saying: Fulfill your work (Ex. 5:13). 11.
[THOU, AND THE LEVITE, AND THE STRANGER.] This means you are obligated to cheer them up with the fruit of your land.
OF TITHING. La-ser (of tithing) is a hifil . It has no neighbor.
WHICH IS THE YEAR OF TITHING. The reference is to the poor tithe.
UNTO THE LEVITE, TO THE STRANGER, TO THE FATHERLESS. To any one of them that you wish.
I HAVE PUT AWAY THE HALLOWED THINGS. The reference is to the tithe. I have also not deposited it. On the contrary, I have handed it over to the one I am obligated to give it to.
I HAVE NOT TRANSGRESSED. Deliberately.
NEITHER HAVE I FORGOTTEN THEM. I did not forget to take the tithes from my house. Or its meaning is, I did not forget to give the two tithes.

I HAVE NOT EATEN THEREOF IN MY MOURNING. The word oni (my mourning) is similar to the word oni (sorrow) in ben-oni (the son of my sorrow) (Gen. 35:18) and onim (mourners) in bread of mourners (Hosea 9:4). I alluded to its meaning in Hebrew. The meaning of oni is, my mourning. If I was in mourning then I did not eat of it before setting aside the tithe.
NEITHER HAVE I PUT AWAY THEREOF. This means neither did I destroy any of that which was holy.
BEING UNCLEAN. Be-tame (being unclean) means for something unclean.

FOR THE DEAD. For the need of the dead. Others say the reference is to idol worship. These things are enumerated because it is prohibited to use the grain for any purpose before giving of the tithe which is holy. If he gives from the remainder he is acting disrespectfully. This is certainly so if he exchanges it for something unclean. As I kept myself and I kept the grain, that is, I removed that which is holy from my house, so may our God watch over our country. This is the meaning of and the land (v. 15).
[A LAND FLOWING WITH MILK AND HONEY.] It means a land that will always flow with milk and honey.
THIS DAY. These are the words of Moses.
THOU SHALT THEREFORE OBSERVE. In your heart.
AND DO THEM. In the land.

THOU HAST AVOUCHED. He’emarta (avouched) means exalted. It is close in meaning to amir (uppermost bough) in In the top of the uppermost bough (Is. 17:6). Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi, who rests in Eden, says that the word is related to va-yomer (said). Its meaning is, you were so righteous that the Lord said He is your God. God likewise acted very righteously towards you that you said that you would be His own treasure. He explained well. Now the word he’emarta is a hifil .
AND TO MAKE THEE HIGH. This is the reward for extolling God.
AND MOSES…COMMANDED. By the dictate of God.
AND THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL. He said this to lighten his load. There are many such instances. I have previously noted them.

KEEP ALL THE COMMANDMENTS. Namely, that thou shalt set thee up great stones to contain the entire Torah. The Gaon, of blessed memory, said that the commandments were listed upon the stones, as in the Halakhot Gedolot . They were listed in a manner similar to the azharot . He explained well.
[WITH PLASTER] Plaster was employed so that it would last.

THAT THOU MAYEST. For God will aid you if you begin to observe His commandments. This first precept upon entering the Land of Israel, namely, the command to build a new altar, was to give thanks to God for their starting to inherit the land.
VERY PLAINLY. The reference is to the writing.
AND MOSES AND THE PRIESTS THE LEVITES. This is in keeping with Scripture’s statement, and the elders of Israel (v. 1). Moses was the main one.
KEEP SILENCE. The meaning of the word hasket (keep silence) can only be known from its context, for it has no neighbor.
THIS DAY THOU ART BECOME A PEOPLE. For God will make a covenant with you.
THOU SHALT THEREFORE HEARKEN. Today, to His voice.
AND DO HIS COMMANDMENTS. In the future.

Scripture mentions the priests and the Levites (v. 9), for they are the ones who said, Cursed be the man (v. 15). The children of the main wives stood over the blessings, while the children of the handmaids stood over the curse. Now if the latter lacked two, the sons of Leah were numerous, and her oldest and youngest were taken.

AND THE LEVITES SHALL SPEAK. Ve-anu (shall speak) is similar to ve-anita (and thou shalt speak) in And thou shalt speak and say (Deut. 26:5). Our rabbis, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of to bless is to say, blessed is the man who does not make a graven or molten image , and similarly all of them. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, the blessing refers to Blessed shalt thou be in the city (Deut. 28:3). The curse is the reverse of this. Proof of this is found in the Book of Joshua.

Scripture mentions these eleven sins because an individual can commit them in secret. And setteth it up in secret (v. 15) is proof, for if one commits this crime in the open he is put to death. He that smiteth his neighbor in secret (v. 24) is similar. Scripture begins with the most important, namely, that which concerns a person and his creator. It then speaks of a person and his parents, for who knows if he dishonors them.
DISHONORETH. The word makleh (dishonoreth) means to dishonor. It is a transitive verb.
CURSED BE HE THAT REMOVETH HIS NEIGHBOR’S LANDMARK. For it is done in secret. [MAKETH THE BLIND TO GO ASTRAY.] Likewise it is not possible for the blind person to identify the one who led him astray.

CURSED BE HE THAT PERVERTETH THE JUSTICE DUE TO THE STRANGER, FATHERLESS. For they have no one to help them. Look, this too is done in secret. Scripture mentions the stranger as well as the orphan and the widow because if the judge perverts the justice due others, they will accuse and publicize him. The stranger, the orphan, and the widow are powerless. Sleeping with one’s father’s wife, with a sister, or with a mother-in-law is an act that is committed in secret, for one is not suspected when he is alone with any one of them. It is not so with other sins.

CURSED BE HE THAT LIETH WITH ANY MANNER OF BEAST. Male or female, for neither have a mouth with which to cry out and protest. Thus, a female animal is like a male animal; therefore Scripture does not mention the male.
HE THAT TAKETH A BRIBE. According to many the reference is to the judge. According to my opinion the reference is to a false witness.

THAT CONFIRMETH NOT. Some say that the reference is to the entire Torah. Others say that it refers to the specifically mentioned sins. However, what they say is meaningless, for Scripture says, to do them . However, it appears to me that Scripture cursed the violators of the precepts which are mentioned. It also cursed the one who secretly does not observe the positive commandments. Scripture therefore reads, to do them .
ON HIGH ABOVE ALL THE NATIONS OF THE EARTH. This is a general blessing. It states that there will be no nation in the world like you.
[AND…SHALL COME.] The meaning of And…shall come is that they shall come by themselves.
AND OVERTAKE THEE. Even though you do not pursue them. It means that you will not tire yourself.
IN THE CITY. This is a blessing regarding an increase in merchandise.
IN THE FIELD. In seeding and planting.
THE FRUIT OF THY BODY. Sons. The word beten (body) is a euphemism.
THE INCREASE OF…AND THE YOUNG. I have previously explained the meaning of these two phrases.
THY BASKET. The place of bread. Thy basket precedes and thy kneading trough but should come after it. On the other hand, thy basket may refer to the place where the flour is placed.

WHEN THOU GOEST OUT. To celebrate festivals, to engage in business, and to take spoil, or in all your daily comings and goings. Its meaning is, you shall be successful in all that you do. The reverse is written [in the curses].

[THAT RISE UP AGAINST THEE.] Since Scripture earlier stated that God will set Israel on high above the nations (v. 1), it now goes on to say that should the nations revolt against Israel [the Lord will cause thine enemies] that rise up against thee [to be smitten before thee].
AND…SEVEN. This means many. The number seven is employed because of the continuous cycle of seven days of the week. It has a set number of days because is contingent on the bodies which are on high.
IN THY BARNS. Ba-asamekha (in thy bams) is in your storehouses. Its meaning is determined by its context.
FOR A HOLY PEOPLE. Holy by observing God’s commandments.
The meaning of yekimekha is, will establish thee.
SHALT KEEP. In your heart.
AND WALK. Practice.
AND…WILL MAKE THEE OVERABUNDANT. The meaning of and will make thee overabundant is, if evil comes to the world, if hunger or blight comes, you will be set aside for good.

HIS…TREASURE. Which is potentially ready in heaven to go out. Compare, the treasuries of the snow (Job 38:22). Scripture speaks of rain after stating will make thee overabundant , for the withholding of rain is the cause of famine.
AND THOU SHALT LEND UNTO MANY NATIONS. For they shall suffer famine. However, no time shall come where you shall borrow. The sum of the matter is, you will always be on top.

IF THOU SHALT HEARKEN. In your heart to observe and to do. The sum of the matter is, do not turn aside from God to serve idols, for the root of all sins is to deny God. The reverse of the aforementioned is to affirm that the Lord is one and to hearken and to observe, for the most important aspect of hearkening is observing.
CURSING. Diminution.
DISCOMFITURE. A state wherein one can not finish what he has started.
REBUKE. A state in which one cannot enjoy what he has worked for, but is concerned for it after he has toiled.
CONSUMPTION. Some say that shachefet (consumption) refers to various types of illnesses.

WITH FEVER. Each day. Kaddachat (fever) is related to kadechah (kindled) in For a fire is kindled (Deut. 32:22). The words mehumah (discomfiture), migeret (rebuke), shachefet (consumption), kaddachat (fever) and dalleket (inflammation) are adjectives.
Dalleket refers to a fever which comes every third or fourth day.
AND WITH FIERY HEAT. The word charchur (fiery heat) is related to the word charah (bum) in and the bottom thereof may burn (Ezek. 24:11).
AND WITH DROUGHT. The word cherev (drought) is related to the word chorev (dry).
AND WITH BLASTING. Shiddafon (blasting) means bloating. Compare, shedufot kadim (blasted with the east wind) (Gen. 41:23). Others say the reverse is true. Its meaning is then thin.

AND WITH MILDEW. Yerakon (mildew) is to be rendered according to its meaning in Arabic. Some say that these refer to diseases of the seed. U-vashiddafon (blasting) is similar to shidufot (blasted) in blasted with the east wind (Gen. 41:23). I have smitten you with blasting (shiddafon) and mildew (Amos 4:9) is proof. Therefore Scripture afterwards reads, and thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass . We find the same in the Torah portion If Ye Walk in My Statutes (Lev. 26:3).
BRASS. Like brass. The same applies to iron.
POWDER AND DUST. Because of the great dryness and the power of the winds.
UNTIL THOU BE DESTROYED. Hishamedakh (thou be destroyed) is irregular. Compare, hibbare’akh (in the day that thou wast created) (Ezek. 28:15).
A HORROR. Some of the letters of za’avah (horror) are reversed. Compare, keves (lamb) and kesev (lamb).
AND THERE SHALL BE NONE TO FRIGHTEN THEM AWAY. To frighten away the birds and beasts.
[THE BOIL OF EGYPT.] Those who remain will be struck with the boil of Egypt.

AND WITH THE EMERODS. They appear in the hidden places. Scripture therefore reads u-vafolim (and with the emerods). The latter is related to the world ofel (hill) in And when he came to the hill (II Kings 5:24).
AND WITH THE SCAB. The same is true in Arabic.

AND WITH THE ITCH. Some say that he will need a potsherd as Job did. This is so even though the word cheres (itch) is spelled with a samekh . Others say u-ve-chares (and with the itch) means: and with a blow from the sun. However, the correct interpretation is that cheres (itch) refers to the name of a disease like the ones mentioned previously. The word has no neighbor.
MADNESS…] Madness, blindness, and astonishment are afflictions of the heart.
AND THOU SHALT GROPE. In blindness.
PROSPEROUS. Tatzli’ach (prosperous) is a transitive verb.
OPPRESSED AND ROBBED. By the enemy, and there shall be none to save thee. Scripture commences to explain in what manner Israel shall be oppressed.
SHALL LIE WITH HER. Yishgalennah (lie with her) is a euphemism for sexual intercourse. The same applies to the word shegal (the queen) (Ps. 45:10). It refers to a woman prepared for bed.
USE THE FRUIT THEREFOF. Techallennu (use the fruit thereof) is related to the word chalil (flute).

AND FAIL WITH LONGING. The word kalot (fail with longing) is similar to the word kaletah (pineth) in My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth (Ps. 84:3) and to va-tekhal (failed with longing) in va-tekhal david (and caused David to fail with longing) (II Sam. 13:39). The latter is not lacking the word “soul” as the one lacking in knowledge says, for the word vatekhal is transitive. The subject is omitted, as it is in “whom she bore” (Num. 26:59).
AND CRUSHED. Powerfully so.
MAD. This explains with madness (v. 28.). He will see his body covered with boils (v. 35).
IN THE KNEES, AND IN THE LEGS. For when the boils are upon the knees and the legs, [it is hard to remove them].
WHEREOF THOU CANST NOT BE HEALED. Because they are on the surface of the body.
AND THERE SHALT THOU SERVE. And it shall not avail you but you shall become an astonishment. That is, all who see you shall be astonished.
A PROVERB. In the ear.
AND A BYWORD. In the mouth. Sheninah (byword) is related to the word ve-shinnantam (and thou shalt teach them diligently) (Deut. 6:7).
SHALL LEAD THEE. Because of your sins. However, before this, a year of hunger shall come upon you when you are still in your land.
SHALL CONSUME THEM. Yachselennu (shall consume them) means shall destroy them. Yachselennu comes from chasil , which is the name of a type of grasshopper.
PLANT. You shall toil in planting and in the vineyards.
BUT THOU SHALT NEITHER DRINK OF THE WINE. At the time of the harvest.
NOR GATHER THE GRAPES. Te’egor (gather the grapes) means you will gather. It is a verb. Te’egor is similar to agerah (gathereth) in And gathereth her food in the harvest (Prov. 6:8).
BUT THOU SHALT NOT ANNOINT THYSELF WITH THE OIL. As is the practice. Compare, neither did I anoint myself at all (Dan. 10:3). This is the reverse of And let thy head lack no oil (Eccles. 9:8).
SHALL DROP OFF. Yishal (drop off) is a nifal .
SHALL…POSSESS. Yeyaresh (shall possess) is a pi’el. Yeyaresh is similar to le-horish (to drive out) in to drive out nations (Num. 4:38).
THE LOCUST. Tzelatzal (locust) is a quadriliteral. It has no neighbor. Its meaning is according to its place.
HIGHER AND HIGHER. The word is repeated to indicate a height over which no one else towers. On the other hand it may indicate permanency. Lower and lower is similar. Its meaning is very low.
HE SHALL BE THE HEAD. As in And the borrower is servant to the lender (Prov. 22:7).

FOR A SIGN. From God, so that you remember that you rebelled against Him. It will not only be a sign in you but also in your offspring, as in Our fathers have sinned, and are not (Lam. 5:7). I have previously explained this.
BY REASON OF THE ABUNDANCE OF ALL THINGS. Which you desired, or all your needs.
SWOOPETH DOWN. Yideh (swoopeth down) means flies. Compare, va-yede (he did swoop down) in Yea, He did swoop down upon the wings of the wind (Ps. 18:11).
AND THOU SHALT EAT THE FRUIT OF THINE OWN BODY. During the siege.
SHALL STRAITEN THEE. Each one of your enemies. Or the word oyevekha is so vocalized because it comes at the end of a verse.
WHOM HE HATH REMAINING. This refers to the enemy. Or it means which he will leave over by hiding them. All of this will he due to the siege.
IN ALL THY GATES. In any place.
AND AGAINST HER AFTERBIRTH. Shilyah (afterbirth) refers to the place where the child dwells while in the mother’s belly.
FROM BETWEEN HER FEET. This is a euphemism. Compare, and he had neither dressed his feet (II Sam. 19:25).
THY PLAGUES. Makkotekha (thy plagues) is a compound of a singular and the plural. Compare, the word edoti (my testimony) in And My testimony that I shall teach them (Ps. 132:12).
The meaning of ve-hifla (will make wonderful) is, it will be an extraordinary thing, for nothing like it was ever seen or heard of.
OF LONG CONTINUANCE. They will not be removed.

WILL THE LORD BRING UPON. Yalem (will bring) is related to the word he’elah (brought up) (Jer. 16:15) even though it is vocalized with a sheva . Others say that yalem means will bring. It is an Aramaic word.
AS THE LORD REJOICED. You should not think that this will harm God or that God will mourn. Its meaning is similar to If thou he righteous, what givest thou to him (Job 35:7).
AND YE SHALL BE PLUCKED. Ve-nissachtem (and ye shall be plucked) is a nifal . It is lacking a nun . It is related to the word yissach (will pluck) in The Lord will pluck up (Prov. 15:25).
SHALL HANG. The word telu’im (shall hang) has an alef in place of the stem heh .

AND…YE SHALL SELL YOURSELVES. Ve-hitmakkartem (and ye shall sell yourselves) does not mean and you will be sold. It means you, both men and women, will seek to sell yourselves and no man shall buy you. Observe, this covenant was made by the command of God in the plains of Moab.
AND MOSES CALLED UNTO ALL ISRAEL. To establish a covenant. Scripture therefore reads afterwards, Ye are standing this day (v. 9).

The reason Scripture reads Ye have seen and then And I have led (v. 4) and then And Og…came out (v. 6) is that some of the Israelites saw the signs that God showed in Egypt, and they and those who came after them saw the miracle of the manna, for they ate no food aside from the manna. And these sons saw that God helped them and they smote two kings (v. 6).
[BUT THE LORD HATH NOT GIVEN YOU A HEART TO KNOW.] Scripture reads a heart to know because they tested God ten times and did not make mention of the signs which they witnessed.
Scripture reads given because God is the first cause. Furthermore, they saw that they had no need for bread or wine.
[ARE NOT WAXEN OLD.] I have previously explained this. Sihon and Og were recently defeated. You are therefore obligated to keep the covenant.
THAT YE MAY…PROSPER. Taskilu means prosper. It is a hifil as the word ta’asun (all that ye do) proves. Compare, maskil (great success) in And David had great success in all his ways (I Sam. 18:14).
YE ARE STANDING THIS DAY. Around the ark.

YOUR HEADS. Roshekhem (your heads) is similar to ha ohelah (the tent) in into the tent Sarah his mother (Gen. 24:67) and even the prophecy, Odad the prophet (II Chron. 15:8). Roshekhem shivtekhem (your heads, your tribes) is to be interpreted as your heads, who are the heads of your tribes. Roshekhem (your heads) is like the word va-niram (we have shot at them) (Num. 21:30). The word is to be so interpreted for the princes were closest to the ark. After them came the elders, followed by the officers, after whom came all the men of Israel, that is, the males, followed by the male little ones, after whom came the women, followed by the strangers.

THAT THOU SHOULDEST ENTER INTO THE COVENANT. Le-ovrekha (that thou shouldest enter) is an infinitive. It is like va-ya’avru (and passed) in and passed between the parts thereof (Jer. 34:18). Observe, the word avar (passed) minus the bet has the opposite meaning.
NEITHER WITH YOU ONLY. But with you and with those who come after you, namely, your sons and your sons’ sons.
[BUT WITH HIM THAT STANDETH HERE WITH US THIS DAY.] The nun of yeshno (that standth here) is superfluous.

AND ALSO WITH HIM THAT IS NOT HERE WITH US. Ve’et asher ennnu (and also with him that is not) means with him that is not here with us but will come after us. It is not to be interpreted as those who say that the spirits of the coming generations were there.
FOR YE KNOW. There are among you some who witnessed the abominations of Egypt, namely, their gods. Additionally, all of you have seen the abominations of the nations.
WHICH YE PASSED. Among them, namely, the Edomites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, and the Midianites.
[A ROOT THAT BEARETH GALL AND WORMWOOD.] For gall injures the healthy. It is a disease that is infectious.
THIS CURSE. This curse refers to Cursed be the man that maketh a graven or molten image (Deut. 27:15).

THAT HE BLESS HIMSELF IN HIS HEART. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi, of blessed memory, says that he bless himself is to be taken according to its plain meaning. When he hears the curse he will bless himself in his heart and say I shall have peace. In other words, when he hears the ban he will say it will not fall on me but upon someone else.

THAT…BE SWEPT AWAY. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi, who rests in paradise, says that the word sefot (swept away) means to extirpate. Compare, tispeh [thou (wilt) sweep away] in Wilt Thou indeed sweep away (Gen. 18:23). In other words, the one who blesses himself wants to nullify the words of the righteous, who are metaphorically called “the watered,” with the words of “the dry.” Look, the righteous are called watered. Compare, For he shall be like a tree planted by the streams of water (Jer. 17:8). The wicked are called dry. Compare, For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert ( Ibid. , v. 6). The wicked person thinks that the blessing which he utters in his heart will also stop the curse. He explained well were it not that the word ravah (well watered) is an adjective. Our text should have read, ravi et ha-tzama (the well watered…with the dry). Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that it means because the corrupt sees the righteous destroyed along with the wicked he therefore thinks evil in his heart. However, this is incorrect because Scripture reads, I shall have peace . In my opinion the word sefot (swept) means to add. Compare, sefot chattat (add sin) (Is. 30:1). The added sin is the wicked person’s statement, I shall have peace even though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart. I will live because of the righteousness of the righteous, for the pious are many and I am an individual sinner. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, The Lord will not be willing to pardon him but then… (v. 19). The meaning of the latter is he shall immediately be destroyed. This verse is also proof of my interpretation of and he shall be forgiven (Num. 15:28). The meaning of sefot is that the well watered will add to the dry. Scripture compares the righteous to the well watered, as in And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water (Ps. 1:3). It compares the wicked to the dry. Compare, For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert (Jer. 17: 6). The fact that Scripture at first reads, a root that beareth gall and wormwood (v. 17), is proof of this. It is in a dry place.

THE ANGER OF THE LORD…SHALL BE KINDLED. The fire of God’s anger shall bum him to the point where the smoke will be visible. Observe, if the sinner be an individual he will die immediately, and if it is a family all the curse…shall lie upon him . This means that the curse shall lie upon the family until its name is eradicated. If the sinner be a tribe, the Lord shall separate him unto evil (v. 20). Similarly And I will offer it up for a burnt-offering (Jud. 11:31), as I have explained.
AND THE GENERATION TO COME. Your children. Also the foreigners who see the plagues of the land.

BRIMSTONE. A prayer to God that all the land should be burnt in brimstone and salt like the overthrow of the places that are mentioned. Some explain that even all the nations shall say (v. 23) repeats what was stated earlier because Scripture went off on a tangent, as is the style of the language. [24.] THEN MEN SHALL SAY. The earlier inhabitants.
[THE GOD OF THEIR FATHERS.] They forsook the God that they and their fathers knew and they served gods whom they did not know.
AND THAT HE HAD NOT ALLOTTED UNTO THEM. I have previously explained this.
AND THE LORD ROOTED THEM OUT. Va-yitteshem (and rooted them out) is missing a nun. Compare li-netosh (to root out) (Jer. 1:10). The nun is swallowed by the dagesh , as is the rule.
[AS IS THIS DAY.] These are the words of the respondents.
THE SECRET THINGS. The reference is to one who serves idols in secret.

BELONG UNTO THE LORD OUR GOD. Its meaning is that his punishment is in the hands of God, and the Lord will exact punishment from him. However, if the sin was committed in public there is an obligation on us and our children to do in accordance with that which is written in the Torah. Others say that the secret and the revealed things belong to God. It is incumbent upon us only to observe the words of the Torah. Now this interpretation has no head or foot. What reason is there to mention this here? Scripture states that if you return unto the Lord (Deut. 30:2), God will turn thy captivity ( Ibid. , v. 3) even though you are outside of the land because it stated earlier, and cast them into another land (v. 27). According to Rabbi Judah the first grammarian, the meaning of ve-shav (then shall turn) (Deut. 30:3) means God will give rest; that is, he will give rest to the captives and be merciful to them, and after this He will return and gather.
IN THE UTTERMOST PARTS OF HEAVEN. With regard to the Land of Israel.

AND THE LORD THY GOD WILL CIRCUMCISE. For He is the first cause of all actions. After saying, you shall return unto the Lord and listen to His voice, Moses says that unlike the circumcision of the flesh, which you are obligated to execute, God will help you and will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed.
[AND THE LORD THY GOD WILL MAKE THEE OVERABUNDANT.] Scripture states ve-hotirekha (make thee overabundant) because God will place curses upon the enemies [of Israel]
AS HE REJOICED OVER THY FATHERS. Who inherited the land, for Scripture addresses those who were exiled from it.

WHICH ARE WRITTEN IN THIS BOOK OF THE LAW. For the main part of all the commandments is there, although they need the explanation provided by tradition. They cannot be kept unless the heart is complete. Scripture therefore states, with all thy heart , for the commandment to keep means to keep with one’s heart.
TOO HARD. The word niflet (too hard) means concealed. Or its meaning is, wondrous, that is, something that will cause you to grow weary while trying to accomplish it.
IT IS NOT IN HEAVEN. This explains niflet (too hard) (v. 11).
BEYOND THE SEA. This explains neither is it far off (v. 11). It is possible that the reference is to the great sea whose width a person cannot enter because of the darkness of the water.

IN THY MOUTH, AND IN THY HEART. For the heart is the core of the commandments. Some commandments require the uttering of statements which serve to reinforce the heart. Others consist of deeds so that a person will utter the required statements.
LIFE. Long life.
AND GOOD. Wealth, bodily health and honor.
Death and evil are the reverse of the above.
TO LOVE. This is most important.
TO WALK IN HIS WAYS. You shall not modify the way He asked you to act and the precepts which He commanded you, even though you do not know why the statutes and ordinances were given.
Note, Then thou shalt live explains the term life (v. 15).
AND MULTIPLY. This explains and good (v. 15), for it refers to material increase, that is, in children and in wealth.
BUT IF THY HEART TURN AWAY. For the heart is most important.
BUT SHALT BE DRAWN AWAY. I have previously explained the meaning of ve-niddachta (but shall be drawn away).
THAT YE SHALL SURELY PERISH. This explains death and evil (v. 15), for they and their children and their wealth shall perish.
YE SHALL NOT PROLONG YOUR DAYS. The reverse of the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land (v. 16).
HEAVEN AND EARTH. For they endure. Similarly with regard to this stone shall be a witness against us (Josh. 24:27) and Hear, O ye mountains, the Lord’s controversy (Micah 6:2).
LIFE AND DEATH. The reference is to the blessing and the curse . Observe, it is incumbent upon you to choose life.
THAT THOU MAYEST LIVE. Physically or in memory. Scripture explains that life is to love.

FOR THAT IS THY LIFE. According to the commentaries this refers to the voice of God. I believe that the reference is to God, as the poet says, the Lord is my salvation; The God of my mercy (Ps. 59:11); My shield (Ps. 18:3); and my sword.

AND MOSES WENT. Moses went to each tribe and tribe to inform them that he was about to die and that they should not fear. He strengthened them with his words to Joshua. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, and thou shalt cause them to inherit it (v. 7). I believe that he then blessed the tribes. This is so even though the blessings are recorded later.

GO OUT AND COME IN. In war. Even if I did not die now, I would not have the ability to wage war. You have no need for any person to help you, for God will destroy the nations. Joshua will do the same. What you saw with your eyes in the war of Sihon and Og is proof.
AND YE SHALL DO UNTO THEM. To break their pillars.
BE STRONG AND OF GOOD COURAGE. Now that you know that God goes with you wherever you go to battle.
BE STRONG AND OF GOOD COURAGE. Moses also said this to Joshua whom he appointed over them.
FOR THOU SHALT GO WITH THIS PEOPLE. The word et means with.
AND DELIVERED IT UNTO THE PRIESTS THE SONS OF LEVI. Who teach the Torah.
AND UNTO ALL THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL. The Sanhedrin. Or its meaning is like And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded (Deut. 27:1).
AT THE END OF EVERY SEVEN YEARS. At the beginning of the year.
THAT THEY MAY LEARN. The entire year. Similarly on the Sabbath.
AND THY STRANGER. Perhaps he will convert to Judaism.
[THAT THEY MAY HEAR, AND THAT THEY MAY LEARN.] When they hear they will ask. And he who is not wise and the children who are young will learn.
THY DAYS APPROACH THAT THOU MUST DIE. For there is a time set for each and everyone. I have previously explained this.
AND MOSES…WENT. From the camp of Israel, for that is where he was. He then came to the camp where God’s presence rested.

AND THE LORD APPEARED IN THE TENT. The specified tent. The meaning of our verse is that the pillar of cloud was at the door of the tent and God was seen inside the tent. This is what the glory refers to. The statement that I may give him a charge (v. 14) refers to And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge (v. 23) by the command of God, may He be blessed. Scripture therefore reads, which I swore unto them ( Ibid. ). After this came the passage Behold, thou art about to sleep with thy fathers (v. 16). There is no chronological order in the Torah. The passage And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law (v. 24) is connected to And Moses wrote this law (v. 9).
AND THIS PEOPLE WILL RISE UP. It is not possible for this to be connected to what precedes it, for what reason is there to say, and this people will rise up, and go astray .
The meaning of ve-zanah (and go astray) is, to leave God’s authority in one’s thought.

AFTER THE FOREIGN GODS OF THE LAND. We know that God is one. Change comes from the recepients. God does not change His works, for they are executed in wisdom. It is part of the service of God to harness one’s power to receive spiritual inspiration in accordance with the place. Scripture therefore reads, the manner of the God of the land (II Kings 17:26). Jacob therefore said, Put away the strange gods (Gen. 35:2). The place is unlike other places with regard to engaging in sexual intercourse with women whom Scripture deems as being of close flesh. The intelligent will understand.

[AMONG THEM.] Be-kirbo (among them) refers to foreign . Scripture, as it were, states, and go astray after the gods of a foreign people, who are the gods of the land. However, it appears that be-kirbo refers to the word ha-aretz (of the land), for the word eretz is found in the masculine. Compare, And the land (ha-aretz) was not able to bear (nasa) them (Gen. 13:6); the land [is] burnt up (netam aretz) (Is. 9:18).
AND I WILL FORSAKE THEM. All of them.
AND THEY SHALL BE. Each one of them shall be food for the enemy.

[AND I WILL SURELY HIDE.] The meaning of And I will surely hide is, if they call Me, I will not answer. Scripture compares God to a person who does not see or know what is happening. It is the custom of Scripture to employ two verbs. Those who know grammar understand this.
IN THAT THEY ARE TURNED. This, as I previously explained, is the great evil. There is no evil which tops it.
NOW…WRITE THIS. A commandment that Moses, and all who know how to write, should write it.
AND TEACH THOU IT. Explain to them the difficult meanings.
PUT IT IN THEIR MOUTHS. That they should be able to recite it orally.
The words ve-lammedah (and teach thou it) and also simah (put it) are irregular, for grammatically the heh of ve-lammedah should have been vocalized with a kamatz and the lamed with a segol .

A WITNESS…AGAINST THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. This meaning of our verse is tied to For when I shall have brought them (v. 20). It is also possible that our verse is independent, because Scripture states, ve-anetah (that…shall testify) (v. 21). Ve-anetah (that…shall testify) is similar to ta’aneh (bear) in thou shalt not bear…against thy neighbor (Ex. 20: 13). The song, as it were, will testify before those who ask, “Why did all this happen to us?”
BEFORE THEM. Le-fanav means before them. It means that the witness will not be removed from before them but shall always be with them.
FOR I KNOW THEIR IMAGINATION. For even if I did not know the future, I know what they have done until this day.
THE SAME DAY. Moses did not tarry in doing this thing. It is possible that this took place on the day he died, which was after writing the words of the Torah, for Moses wrote the song with it.
UNTIL THEY WERE FINISHED. This is connected to the words .
THAT MOSES COMMANDED THE LEVITES. Scripture is being brief. Our verse, as it were, says, the earlier-mentioned Levites who are kohanim , but not all the Levites, for they do not touch the ark.
[THAT BORE THE ARK OF THE CONVENT OF THE LORD.] By command. There are many such instances.

IT MAY BE THERE FOR A WITNESS AGAINST THEE. Moses speaks to all of Israel. The kohanim are included when he speaks to Israel. However, when Moses addressed the Reubenites and the Gadites he spoke to them alone, as I previously explained.

AND HOW MUCH MORE AFTER MY DEATH. In addition, I know that after my death… for God told me, and this people will rise up, and go astray (v. 16) after you sleep with your fathers. This is what after my death refers to.
[BEFALL YOU.] The meaning of ve-karata (and…will befall you) is similar to ve-chatat (but the fault is) in but the fault is in thine people (Ex. 5:15). It is explained there.
